statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r.val is the length of the last word of s. Formally, let e be the largest index with 0 <= e < len(s) and s[e] != 32. Let a be the smallest index with 0 <= a <= e, s[j] != 32 for every j with a <= j <= e, and (a = 0 or s[a-1] = 32). Then r.val = e - a + 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] = 32 or (65 <= s[i] <= 90) or (97 <= s[i] <= 122); and there exists i with 0 <= i < len(s) and s[i] != 32.
